# 1958–1962: America at the Edge

The summer of 1958 sat at a peculiar hinge point in American history. The euphoria of postwar prosperity had begun to curdle into something more anxious, more complicated. Sputnik's launch the previous October had punctured a bubble of technological complacency that American industry and American confidence had inflated since V-J Day. The Soviet Union had put a satellite in orbit; what did that say about American science, American education, American resolve?
